scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Human Marionettes of Myanmar
This is Burmese dance. 2nd century BC to present.
on_screen: Title card: Burmese dance · Myanmar · 2nd century BC to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Traced to Pyu and Mon cultures from 200 BC, with significant Thai influence following the 1767 sack of Ayutthaya.
Modern codification occurred in 1953 by Oba Thaung at the State School of Music in Mandalay.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Used for spirit propitiation (Nat), devotional offerings to Buddha (Oil Lamp), community fundraising (U Shwe Yoe), and seasonal celebrations like Thingyan.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Characterized by angular, fast-paced movements and a focus on poses.
Includes specific forms like the Oil Lamp dance (upturned hands), Nat dance (frenzied crescendo), and Yein (synchronized group movement).
Watch for Oil Lamp Balance, Zawgyi Prance.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Synchronous group lines (Yein), circular or stage-based duets, and solo ritual spaces.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Accompanied by the Hsaing Waing orchestra or drums.
Music ranges from legato ritual songs to improvised lively tunes for folk dances.
Listen for the Hsaing Waing, Drums, Gongs.
A percussive and reactive soundscape dominated by the Hsaing Waing orchestra, characterized by shifts from slow, sedate tempos in Bagan-style dances to intense, rapid beats for spirit possession.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Legato transitioning to frenzied crescendo in ritual contexts.
scenes.music: the music brief's underscore at its own tempo; drop narration under the hook of a verified recording if licensed, else original

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Varies by character: red silk for Nat mediums, green regal attire for Mount Popa spirits, and wrist-attached wings for Kinnara.
Often performed in temporary bamboo theaters (Zat Pwe) or at pagoda festivals.
on_screen: Image gallery: 8 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Oba Thaung is credited with codifying the repertoire; U Shwe Yoe and Daw Moe are famous fictitious folk characters.
Rakhine people of western Burma are noted for their specific devotional Oil Lamp dances.
Derived from Pyu and Mon traditions; influenced by Thai (Yိုးဒယား) and Khmer court styles; closely linked to Burmese marionette theater.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Burmese dance is parent of Yama Zatdaw: The Burmese version of the Ramayana which introduced Siamese court dance elements.
Burmese dance is sibling of Khon: Thai masked dance which shares historical roots and character types like the demon and monkey.
on_screen: Graph: the connections with their relation labels

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Nat dances involve spirit propitiation and mediumship; offerings of green coconut and bananas are traditionally required before performances to appease the Guardian Spirit of Land.

scenes.title: Until next time
narration: Explore the high-energy world of Burmese dance, where spirit mediums dance to a frenzy and humans mimic the movements of ancient puppets.
